newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWIMMING-HUNGARY OFFICIAL BARRED FOR TWO YEARS OVER PHANTOM MEET.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-HUNGARY OFFICIAL BARRED FOR TWO YEARS OVER PHANTOM MEET.

text.p: World swimming's governing body FINA on Tuesday banned for two years a top official from the Hungarian association in a scandal over a "phantom" meeting.
A statement from the Lausanne-based FINA said the official, the association's secretary-general Joszef Ruza, "has been suspended for two years from any international activity."
At the same time, the a severe warning had been issued to the Hungarian body itself, FINA said.

The move followed allegations last month when it emerged that half the team from Hungary, one of the world's top swimming nations, went to the Atlanta Olympics based on a qualifying competition that never took place.
Tamas Gyarfas, president of the Hungarian association who resigned over the affair but was later re-elected, has denounced the fraud as an "inadmissible, grave mistake."
But he said it did not result in Hungarian swimmers taking the place of any other nation's athletes at the Games as each country had its own quota of places.
Hungary took three gold, one silver and two bronze medals in Atlanta.
Ruza last month took full responsibility for the affair -- in which "results" from a fictitious contest from June 6-8 were forwarded to FINA.
But he insisted that the fraud was international practice and that FINA was aware of what had happened before the Olympics. FINA denied this.
